daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The presidential palace denied allegations that any former leader is interfering with President Prabowo's administration, with the Istana rejecting claims of such meddling. The statement comes amid heightened scrutiny of former President Jokowi's political safari, which began with a visit to Lampung. Political observers described the tour as consolidation for the 2029 legislative elections, while another analyst said the safari opens the door to "Jokowisme 2.0".

  • A political branding expert explained the significance of Jokowi wearing PSI attire as a strategy to preserve and transfer his political influence.
  • The Secretary General of Partai Buruh resigned, with party chairman Said Iqbal stating this was not the first time such a resignation has occurred.
  • President Prabowo told 2,600 rectors and deans that professors hold key government posts to solve national challenges.
  • A ministry is pushing to harmonize the Archipelagic Regions Bill with existing laws.
  • The government reviewed governance of the MBG program, with authorities stating they will prioritize vulnerable groups in the scheme.
  • Coordinating Minister Zulhas acknowledged concerns from BGN partners, saying partners should not be sacrificed.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and France are seeking to strengthen their defense cooperation, with both countries pursuing closer military ties. The initiative comes as Indonesia continues to diversify its defense partnerships beyond traditional allies. Meanwhile, the state energy company Pertamina is monitoring an oil tanker stuck in the Strait of Hormuz amid regional tensions.

  • The CPTPP trade bloc has opened preliminary talks for Indonesia's membership, along with the Philippines and UAE.
  • Pakistan's ambassador said that people-to-people relations are key to strengthening ties with Indonesia.
  • The TNI officially commissioned 1,737 junior officers with the rank of lieutenant.
  • Saudi Arabia invited 1,000 umrah pilgrims from countries worldwide, including from Indonesia.

Other

Indonesia officially began its B50 biodiesel mandate, marking what authorities describe as a new era of energy independence. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources stated that energy transition is a strategic imperative to reduce the country's import burden. The rollout of B50, which blends 50 percent palm oil-based biodiesel with conventional diesel, represents a major step in Indonesia's renewable energy strategy.

  • The government postponed implementation of new airfare caps and will revise them once fuel prices stabilize.
  • The Finance Ministry announced plans to deploy oversight teams for MBG funds across the country.
  • The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank will open an Indonesia office after securing US$17 billion in financing.
  • Indonesia is eyeing over US$1 billion from Panda Bond issuance as demand surges.
  • Police charged 287 foreign nationals in a major online gambling bust, with authorities revealing that 15 companies allegedly sponsored the operation at the Hayam Wuruk site.
